The 1983 high-street computer shop from down on the shop floor: the varnished oak counter crosses the foreground with its brass till and the opened straw-filled crate at its near end, the three shelf bays stacked with beige boxed home computers rise behind, cream-and-teal linoleum runs underfoot and daylight washes in from the street door. Framing: the camera is DOWN ON THE SHOP FLOOR at counter height, low, looking ACROSS the counter — the varnished oak counter runs HORIZONTALLY ACROSS THE FULL WIDTH OF THE FOREGROUND as a near edge close to camera, left frame edge to right frame edge, with the room and the three bays filling the space beyond it. The counter does NOT run away from the camera into depth along a side wall. The opened straw-filled crate stands ON THE COUNTER'S NEAR END, at one end of that foreground counter edge and touching it, never on the floor and never at the opposite side of the frame from the counter. Palette: beige, teal, warm oak, cream. A queue of eager buyers stands packed along the far side of the counter and ranked back between the bays, in wide collars and bulky coats, and the head of the queue is pressed to the counter edge. EVERY raised banknote is GRIPPED BY A VISIBLE CARTOON HAND on a visible arm belonging to a buyer in the queue — no banknote floats free in the air without a hand and arm attached. Any in-world lettering that appears must be complete and fully legible, never half-hidden behind a head or cropped to a fragment.

The same lit shop-window display seen from inside: two oversized beige computer cases butted front to front, dented at the corners, the platform scuffed beneath them, the plate glass behind with the crowd of passers-by packed along the pavement on its far side, one spotlight above. Only this changes: two flat black glass phone slabs now STAND VERTICALLY ON END at the front edge of the platform, each one standing upright on its short bottom edge like a domino stood on end or a book shut and stood on a shelf — their two large flat faces pressed together face to face and shoved hard against each other, a matching dent where they meet, their bottom edges skidded apart under the push, locked up in exactly the same head-to-head shoving match as the two cases behind them, at their own smaller scale. The slabs must NOT lie flat on the platform, must NOT lie face-up, and must NOT be splayed open like an opened book. EVERYTHING ELSE IS HELD EXACTLY AS THE SEED FRAME ESTABLISHES IT, re-drawn unchanged: the PLATE GLASS side panels (flat glass, never a wooden proscenium or timber frame), the black platform carrying its RED SCUFFED CONTACT ARC at full strength, the single spotlight above with its cone unchanged, and the two oversized beige cases at their established proportion, dented only at the corners and otherwise unscuffed. The crowd of passers-by beyond the glass is THE SAME CROWD as established — the same people in the same positions packed along the pavement, in bulky 1980s winter coats, headscarves and shopping bags; not a new group, not repositioned, and never in short sleeves, t-shirts or modern casual dress. Red appears ONLY as that scuffed contact arc and nowhere else.
